section_summary: This section traces U.S. policy toward supplying and disposing of goods in Japan from wartime export controls through the post-surrender occupation. Its central subjects are fertilizer and raw-material imports, Foreign Liquidation Commission administration, and the negotiation and implementation of agreements permitting Japan to purchase surplus U.S. military property. Later papers concern reparations equipment, surrendered supplies, vessels, and an internal dispute over using Japanese surplus-property credits to acquire land, with several later or apparently misfiled documents extending through 1949.

subfiles.title: Inquiry concerning prewar shipments of strategic supplies to Japan
subfiles.from: C. Wayland Brooks, U.S. Senate
subfiles.to: Edward R. Stettinius Jr., Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests an official statement on U.S. policy toward prewar exports of scrap iron, aviation articles, designs, and other supplies to Japan, Germany, and Italy.
subfiles.summary: Brooks cites claims State opposed strategic shipments to Japan before controls and asks about aviation designs and samples given to Japan, Germany and Italy.

subfiles.title: Reply on prewar strategic exports to Japan, Germany, and Italy
subfiles.from: Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Directs Brooks to official publications explaining moral embargoes, export controls, and munitions exports before World War II.
subfiles.summary: Reply: before the July 2, 1940 Act, measures were moral embargoes on aircraft, manufacturing materials and aviation-gasoline technology; encloses Peace and War and cites FRUS and Munitions Control Board reports.

subfiles.title: Clarification of Bern telegram on the Japanese Munitions Company Law
subfiles.from: J. A. Williams
subfiles.about: Corrects a misleading interpretation of a German report about expansion of Japan's wartime industrial-control law.
subfiles.summary: Memo: Japan extended its Munitions Company Law in December 1944, covering about 600 companies in Japan, 55 in Korea and 30 in Formosa, versus 150 when enacted in 1943.

subfiles.title: German press report on extension of Japanese armaments controls
subfiles.from: Huddle, Bern
subfiles.about: Reports German press claims concerning the extension of Japanese armaments legislation to Korea and Formosa.
subfiles.summary: German press report: 55 armament companies projected for Korea, 37 Japanese firms with Korean plants already designated, Formosa designations in preparation.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Foreign Economic Administration reports on Japan
subfiles.from: David L. Gordon, Foreign Economic Administration
subfiles.about: Sends a group of FEA reports on Japan and promises a forthcoming report on Japan's minimum import requirements.
subfiles.summary: Gordon sends more Foreign Economic Administration reports than needed so State can choose; the minimum-import-requirements study will follow.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment and forwarding of FEA reports to Tokyo
subfiles.from: Woodbury Willoughby, Department of State
subfiles.to: David L. Gordon, Foreign Economic Administration
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the FEA reports and states that they will be sent by pouch to the Political Adviser in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Willoughby thanks Gordon for the valuable Japan reports and arranges their transmission to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Request to dispatch draft radiogram on raw-silk exports
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin, Department of State
subfiles.to: Colonel J. R. Gilchrist, War Department
subfiles.about: Asks the War Department to send SCAP a draft radiogram concerning exports of raw silk and return a record copy.
subfiles.summary: Martin encloses a draft radiogram on raw-silk exports for SCAP and asks the final War Department message for the file.

subfiles.title: Missing forms for the Calcutta stockpile
subfiles.from: Johnson, Yokohama
subfiles.to: Department of State, attention McCabe, FLC
subfiles.about: Reports that supplemental forms concerning the Calcutta stockpile have not arrived by diplomatic air pouch.
subfiles.summary: Johnson says promised supplemental SPH forms for the Calcutta stockpile were not received; telegram received March 12, 1946.

subfiles.title: Request for fertilizer allocations to Japan
subfiles.from: James F. Byrnes, Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Clinton P. Anderson, Secretary of Agriculture
subfiles.about: Urges allocation of phosphate rock and potash salts to Japan to support food production and occupation stability.
subfiles.summary: Byrnes describes chemical-fertilizer shortages as a threat to Japanese crop yields, public order, and the security of occupation forces. He asks the U.S. member of the Combined Fertilizer Committee to recommend April–May allocations equal to at least ten percent of Japan's stated requirements for phosphate rock and potash salts.

subfiles.title: Japanese fertilizer requirements and proposed action
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin
subfiles.about: Analyzes SCAP's fertilizer-import request and recommends diplomatic, military, and production measures to increase supplies.
subfiles.summary: SCAP requested 1,040,000 tons ammonium sulfate, 750,000 phosphate rock and 150,000 potash for 1946; Martin explains shortages and recommends asking Agriculture for token allocations.

subfiles.title: File catch slip for a Sydney paper
subfiles.from: Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.about: Records a request or charge for a specific paper described as A-44 to Sydney.
subfiles.summary: File catch slip for a Sydney paper, file 894.24; administrative only.

subfiles.title: Agriculture Department response on phosphate and potash for Japan
subfiles.from: N. E. Dodd, Acting Secretary of Agriculture
subfiles.about: Reports a phosphate allocation for Japan and explains why no pre-July potash allocation had yet been made.
subfiles.summary: Combined Food Board allocated 100,000 tons of phosphate rock; with other potash committed and most in Germany, occupation authorities for Japan and Germany were asked to explore a transfer.

subfiles.title: War Department proposal for selling surplus supplies to Japanese agencies
subfiles.from: Kenneth C. Royall, Under Secretary of War
subfiles.to: W. L. Clayton, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Defends a proposal for the Foreign Liquidation Commission to sell appropriate surplus military supplies to Japanese agencies.
subfiles.summary: Royall says current transfers burden the theater commander with custody; a formal FLC sale would create deferred Japanese payment and allow disposal of unexportable items; rejects limiting sales to the disease-and-unrest formula.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Royall's surplus-property letter
subfiles.from: W. L. Clayton, Department of State
subfiles.to: Kenneth C. Royall, Under Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Royall's letter on surplus-property sales in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Clayton says Royall's letter helps continuing surplus-property talks; no final policy stated.

subfiles.title: Siamese sale of Japanese military shoe polish
subfiles.from: K. P. Landon, Department of State
subfiles.about: Records allegations that a Siamese government auction of Japanese military shoe polish improperly favored officials.
subfiles.summary: Major Griswold reports a large stock of Kiwi shoe polish sold after minimal publicity at an opening bid of fifteen satangs per tin, prompting protests and demands for investigation.

subfiles.title: Shanghai charges on cargo intended for Hong Kong
subfiles.from: Johnson, Foreign Liquidation Commission
subfiles.about: Requests authority to pay transportation and storage costs caused by accidental unloading at Shanghai of cargo consigned to Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: Shanghai incurred $11,662.16 in transport and storage charges for Hong Kong cargo already paid for; Johnson asks to use local sales receipts or draw on a Shanghai bank; page 21 is the corrected copy.

subfiles.title: Coordination of UNRRA petroleum supply from Pacific military surpluses
subfiles.from: CINCAFPAC, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Recommends using surplus Pacific petroleum products for UNRRA and centralizing coordination through CINCAFPAC's Area Petroleum Officer.
subfiles.summary: The message notes that large stocks of petroleum products were expected to be declared surplus while UNRRA requirements in China were otherwise being purchased locally. It recommends maximum use of military surpluses, commercial storage and distribution contracts, and systematic information exchange among UNRRA, FLC, Navy, and Army petroleum officers.

subfiles.title: Weekly surplus-property statistics from China
subfiles.from: Johnson, FLC, COMGEN USAF China
subfiles.to: Department of State, attention McCabe and Howard
subfiles.about: Transmits coded dollar totals for weekly surplus-property disposal statistics.
subfiles.summary: Weekly surplus-property figures from China for the week ending May 25, without narrative.

subfiles.title: Responses to questions on disposal reports and lend-lease property
subfiles.from: Johnson, FLC
subfiles.about: Answers administrative questions concerning contracts, reporting copies, disposal reports, and returned lend-lease property.
subfiles.summary: Johnson says no delivery lists were attached because contracted property was treated as delivered, no returned lend-lease property was received, and revised reports follow by airmail.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about receipt of Hong Kong payment
subfiles.from: Johnson, COMGEN USAF China
subfiles.about: Seeks confirmation that a $200,000 Hong Kong government payment reached the U.S. Treasury.
subfiles.summary: Hong Kong Government Purchasing Commission sent two bank drafts by Navy courier May 11; Johnson asks immediate notice of receipt.

subfiles.title: National Advisory Council approval of sales to Japan
subfiles.from: Mr. Hemmendinger
subfiles.about: Reports NAC approval of selling disease-and-unrest surplus property to Japan and discusses alternatives for other residual property.
subfiles.summary: National Advisory Council approved payment for surplus property as a first charge on Japanese export proceeds; Category B property the Army cannot economically remove may be destroyed, donated or sold on credit.

subfiles.title: First-quarter budget request for FLC China
subfiles.from: Johnson, FLC, COMGEN USAF China
subfiles.about: Requests a $28,100 budget for the first quarter of fiscal year 1946.
subfiles.summary: Johnson says FLC China budget forms were mailed June 4, concerning operating funds.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about purchasing automobiles for American veterans
subfiles.from: Johnson
subfiles.about: Asks whether a local company of American veterans may purchase 200 automobiles from the War Assets Corporation and pay locally in dollars.
subfiles.summary: Veterans' company asks authority for a War Assets Corporation transaction of about 200 cars after earlier FLC purchases.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to SCAP on abaca, maguey, and flax requirements
subfiles.from: Department of State, signed Acheson acting
subfiles.to: SCAP, Tokyo, for the Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Requests Japanese requirements and payment arrangements for Philippine abaca and maguey and offers Peruvian and Brazilian flax stocks.
subfiles.summary: The Department warns that immediate Philippine production may not sustain 500 tons of abaca per month and asks SCAP to specify essential grades and quantities. It suggests payment from Japanese sales such as silk and lists prices and stocks for Peruvian flax fiber and tow, with additional Brazilian flax available.

subfiles.title: SCAP acknowledgment of raw-fiber inquiry
subfiles.from: SCAP, Tokyo
subfiles.to: War Department for MARCOS and Department of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the August 8 inquiry on abaca and other fibers and promises an early answer.
subfiles.summary: SCAP states that action on State's telegram number 436 is not yet complete. A fuller response will be provided later.

subfiles.title: Forwarding of War Department surplus-property correspondence
subfiles.from: Kenneth C. Royall, Under Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of War Department letters concerning surplus-property policy in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Royall sends copies of letters to Clayton, General Connolly and Harold Glasser, noting coordination with Shenefield and Shields.

subfiles.title: Departmental position on residual surplus items in Japan
subfiles.from: Hale T. Shenefield
subfiles.about: Recommends State Department approval of sales of residual Category C surplus property to Japanese agencies.
subfiles.summary: Ad hoc committee estimates residual property in Japan at about $45 million with $60 million more expected; sales would aid rehabilitation, cut occupation costs and recover value; repayment left to the peace settlement.

subfiles.title: Proposal for disposing of Category C surplus property in Japan
subfiles.from: Kenneth C. Royall, Under Secretary of War
subfiles.to: W. L. Clayton, Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Requests authorization for financial arrangements permitting Japanese agencies to buy residual U.S. military surplus.
subfiles.summary: Royall divides Japanese surplus into occupation needs, items marketable abroad, and Category C uneconomical to remove; selling the residue in Japan cuts costs, curbs inflation and reduces US-financed imports; NAC authority covered only the first.

subfiles.title: Notice to the Deputy Foreign Liquidation Commissioner on proposed Japanese sales
subfiles.from: Kenneth C. Royall, Under Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Advises Connolly that Royall has asked Clayton to facilitate disposal of available Japanese surplus to Japanese agencies.
subfiles.summary: Royall tells the Deputy Foreign Liquidation Commissioner that further study disclosed new facts, enclosing his letter to Clayton on the benefits of the plan.

subfiles.title: Notice to the National Advisory Council secretary on Japanese surplus sales
subfiles.from: Kenneth C. Royall, Under Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Reports renewed action to establish a method for selling surplus property in Japan to Japanese agencies.
subfiles.summary: Royall tells the NAC secretary that FLC and the War Department further studied the program, enclosing his request for a disposal mechanism for surplus in Japan.

subfiles.title: Confirmation of NAC authorization for residual surplus transfers
subfiles.from: Willard L. Thorp, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Kenneth C. Royall, Under Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Confirms the NAC decision authorizing transfer of surplus property beneficial to the occupation of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Thorp quotes the December 16, 1946 NAC action approving transfers that War and FLC judged beneficial to the occupation. Repayment terms were to be determined as part of the Japanese peace settlement, and the War Department was authorized to proceed with FLC.

subfiles.title: Request for Tokyo FLC disbursing and certifying officers
subfiles.from: George Atcheson Jr., Tokyo
subfiles.about: Requests dedicated financial officers for the newly arrived Foreign Liquidation Commission staff in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: James McConnell arrived with about fourteen FLC employees for Tokyo; Atcheson urges transferring the $15,000 allotment and designating FLC certifying and disbursing officers.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal of Yokohama FLC allotment
subfiles.from: Department of State, signed Acheson acting
subfiles.to: Yokohama Branch, Office of the U.S. Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Withdraws $15,000 from the unobligated balance of Yokohama allotment G-136.
subfiles.summary: Telegram continues the remaining first-quarter Yokohama FLC balance through December 31, 1946, with a formal allotment document to follow.

subfiles.title: Correction to Yokohama allotment telegram
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.to: Yokohama Branch, Office of the U.S. Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Corrects the October 7 telegram concerning the Yokohama FLC allotment.
subfiles.summary: Correction: disregard the second sentence of the first paragraph of telegram 98; no replacement given.

subfiles.title: Establishment of Tokyo FLC allotment G-137
subfiles.from: Department of State, signed Acheson acting
subfiles.to: SCAP, Tokyo, for the Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Allots $32,000 for Tokyo Foreign Liquidation Commission operations during October–December 1946.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo FLC allotment G-137 covers most expenses except customer travel and entertainment, accounted under State's advances account.

subfiles.title: Information on newsprint and licensing for Liberty Magazine in Japan
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Department of State
subfiles.to: L. L. Horch, Department of Commerce
subfiles.about: Explains the limited availability of Japanese newsprint and the permissions required for Liberty Magazine to operate in occupied Japan.
subfiles.summary: Whitman says a licensed Liberty Magazine might get a small share of Japanese newsprint but should ship from the US; needs SCAP authorization and a Treasury license; yen contracts with no conversion guarantee.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of information on Japanese newsprint
subfiles.from: L. L. Horch, Department of Commerce
subfiles.to: Roswell H. Whitman, Department of State
subfiles.about: Thanks Whitman for newsprint information requested on behalf of Manufacturers Trust Company.
subfiles.summary: Horch states that the information has been passed to Manufacturers Trust Company. He reports that the company appreciates receiving it.

subfiles.title: Financial procedures for the Tokyo FLC office
subfiles.from: Department of State, signed Acheson acting
subfiles.to: SCAP, Tokyo, for the Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Confirms cancellation of the Yokohama allotment and prescribes embassy certification and disbursement procedures for Tokyo FLC expenses.
subfiles.summary: G-136 for $15,000 was canceled and G-137 for $32,000 established in Tokyo; embassy officers certify and pay FLC-approved vouchers, with the certifying officer responsible for legality.

subfiles.title: Shipment of ex-military communications supplies to China
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman
subfiles.about: Reviews SCAP's shipment of formerly military communications equipment to China and drafts a cautionary reply.
subfiles.summary: SCAP says ex-military communications equipment needed civilian reconditioning before China shipment; Whitman calls it a borderline but supportable case and advises SCAP to take care.

subfiles.title: Despatch reporting authorization for Japanese purchases of U.S. surplus
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAPIN 1313 authorizing the Imperial Japanese Government to purchase approved civilian-type U.S. military surplus.
subfiles.summary: Despatch encloses SCAP memorandum: vehicles and specifically approved civilian-type military supplies may be bought from the Foreign Liquidation Commission.

subfiles.title: SCAP authorization for Japanese purchase of civilian-type military surplus
subfiles.from: John B. Cooley, for the Supreme Commander
subfiles.to: Imperial Japanese Government through the Central Liaison Office
subfiles.about: Authorizes the Japanese government to purchase approved vehicles and other civilian-type U.S. military supplies from FLC.
subfiles.summary: SCAP authorizes Japanese purchases of civilian-type military surplus through contracts with its permission, and direct contact between SCAP sections and designated Japanese agencies.

subfiles.title: Transmission of signed U.S.–Japan credit agreement
subfiles.from: Chester M. Carre, Office of the Foreign Liquidation Commissioner
subfiles.about: Sends the Treaty Branch an executed credit agreement and supporting SCAP documents for filing.
subfiles.summary: Carre transmits the signed US-Japan credit agreement with SCAP's approval certified by Marquat and Cooley's November 9 letter; asks Barron to acknowledge.

subfiles.title: Letter agreement governing Japanese purchases of U.S. surplus property
subfiles.from: William E. Vogelback, Central Field Commissioner for Pacific and China
subfiles.about: Establishes basic terms for Japanese purchase of approved U.S. surplus property, accepted by K. Tsukada and certified by SCAP.
subfiles.summary: FLC agrees to sell SCAP-approved civilian-type supplies for dollars on War Department import terms, with terms negotiated in the field; K. Tsukada accepted for Japan, Marquat certified.

subfiles.title: SCAP transmittal of executed surplus-property agreement
subfiles.from: John B. Cooley, for the Supreme Commander
subfiles.to: Assistant Field Commissioner for China and Eastern Asia, OFLC
subfiles.about: Returns executed copies of the general agreement for selling U.S. surplus property to the Japanese government.
subfiles.summary: SCAP letter: Tsukada executed and Marquat certified the agreement; the Japanese representative kept the original, and a duplicate and two copies went to OFLC.

subfiles.title: Report on truck sales and regulation of Japanese surplus purchases
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports that FLC had sold 2,150 U.S. Army trucks to Japan and transmits regulations governing purchased surplus property.
subfiles.summary: Despatch on truck sales: SCAPIN 1384 sets marking, registration and use rules for the surplus property, to be implemented by the Japanese government.

subfiles.title: Payroll refund for Billie J. Tim
subfiles.from: Department of State, signed Byrnes
subfiles.to: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo, attention OFLC
subfiles.about: Instructs the Tokyo office to send a payroll refund to Billie J. Tim.
subfiles.summary: Airgram on a payroll refund for Billie Tim: biweekly bond deduction $9.38; send money order for net refund of $47.82.

subfiles.title: Transmission of November 22 U.S.–Japan surplus-property agreement
subfiles.from: Chester M. Carre, Office of the Foreign Liquidation Commissioner
subfiles.about: Sends a signed duplicate of the November 22 agreement between the United States and Japan for treaty-file purposes.
subfiles.summary: Carre transmits the November 22 US-Japan surplus agreement, signed by Hammonds and Tsukada, and requests signed acknowledgment.

subfiles.title: Agreement between the United States and Japan for sale of certain surplus property
subfiles.from: Government of the United States of America
subfiles.about: Creates a bulk-sale framework for Japan to purchase approved U.S. surplus property located in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The agreement anticipates Japanese purchases from an estimated $50 million in surplus property and incorporates the September 3 letter agreement. It excludes fixed installations, aircraft-related equipment, ships, maritime equipment, and non-demilitarized combat materiel, and sets the price at thirty percent of U.S. procurement cost. Property is sold as-is and where-is, with Japan responsible for removal, storage consequences, taxes, and efforts to prevent reimportation into the United States. George S. Hammonds and K. Tsukada signed the agreement, which W. F. Marquat certified as approved by SCAP.

subfiles.title: Rumored supply of U.S. surplus vessels to Germany and Japan
subfiles.from: Mr. Flory, Fisheries and Wildlife Branch
subfiles.about: Records a congressional inquiry about possible transfer of convertible surplus vessels to German and Japanese fishing industries.
subfiles.summary: Linden reports a rumor of US surplus vessels going to Germany and Japan, as Congressman King wants the fishing industry to have first chance; Department knew of a possible German program but no Japanese one.

subfiles.title: Distribution of Japanese farm-land reform information in Argentina
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese farm-land reform information for possible delivery to Argentine authorities and Japanese nationals.
subfiles.summary: Circular airgram: Japanese Foreign Ministry farm-land reform material forwarded from Tokyo for Japanese communities abroad; its application to land owned by United Nations nationals abroad was under SCAP discussion.

subfiles.title: English translation of French note on Japanese naval reparations
subfiles.from: Embassy of France in the United States
subfiles.about: Relinquishes French claims to Japanese warships in favor of naval-yard and naval-base equipment.
subfiles.summary: France concludes that allocated Japanese warships would require costly alterations. It instead requests floating docks, repair ships, mobile-base components, and a yard for constructing and repairing naval equipment, preferably delivered promptly.

subfiles.title: French-language note on Japanese naval reparations
subfiles.from: Ambassade de France aux Etats-Unis
subfiles.about: French original of the note relinquishing claims to Japanese warships and requesting naval-support equipment.
subfiles.summary: The French government states that Japanese warships would be usable only after extensive and costly modification. It asks instead for floating docks, workshop ships, mobile-base elements, and a naval construction and repair yard.

subfiles.title: Sebald warning about proposed amendment of the surplus-property agreement
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.to: James K. Penfield, Department of State
subfiles.about: Warns that a draft SWNCC proposal to use FLC credits for acquiring Japanese land has provoked General MacArthur's vehement opposition.
subfiles.summary: Sebald warns that Larkin's unofficial draft amendment concerns MacArthur, who denied requesting it and calls land acquisition through FLC credits coercive; recommends stopping the SWNCC paper until a peace treaty.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning the unofficial SWNCC surplus-property draft
subfiles.from: James K. Penfield, Office of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Assures Sebald that the controversial paper was only an internal draft and would not gain official status without correction.
subfiles.summary: Penfield says the draft came from Larkin's office with no standing; Northeast Asian office and General Saltzman found serious deficiencies; he will block proposals inconsistent with Japanese realities.

subfiles.title: Despatch on transfer of responsibility for surrendered supplies
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAPIN 1835 transferring Japanese responsibility for surrendered supplies from the former Home Ministry to the Construction Board.
subfiles.summary: Despatch encloses SCAP's December 29 directive reassigning receipt and accounting for surrendered supplies because the Home Ministry was dissolving.

subfiles.title: SCAP directive transferring surrendered-supply records to the Construction Board
subfiles.from: R. M. Levy, for the Supreme Commander
subfiles.to: Japanese Government through the Central Liaison Office
subfiles.about: Designates the Construction Board as successor to the Home Ministry for returned Japanese military supplies and equipment.
subfiles.summary: SCAP directive orders the Construction Board to receive and account for former Japanese armed forces supplies, taking over all Home Ministry records without interruption.

subfiles.title: Telegram concerning lend-lease vessels at Yokohama
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Provides a heavily garbled update concerning lend-lease vessels at Yokohama and an expected arrival.
subfiles.summary: Telegram on lend-lease vessels at Yokohama, citing Washington information; an arrival expected February 28; names and details illegible.

subfiles.title: Condition and disposition of tankers Y-9 and Y-20
subfiles.from: CINCFE, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Department of the Army, with information to COMPHILRYCOM and Department of State
subfiles.about: Reports the repair costs and excess status of tankers Y-9 and Y-20 and requests disposition instructions.
subfiles.summary: Tankers Y-9 and Y-20 are inoperable, needing repairs of $18,000 and $25,000 over ninety days; Far East Command considers them excess and asks if they will be used elsewhere or declared surplus to OFLC.

subfiles.title: Submission of draft reply to Dr. Kan Chieh-hou
subfiles.from: W. Walton Butterworth, Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Forwards a proposed reply to Dr. Kan's urgent requests for further U.S. assistance.
subfiles.summary: Draft reply to Dr. Kan Chieh-hou attached with his October letters; the President apparently saw his October 5 reply as sufficient.

subfiles.title: Summary of NAC action on disposal of military goods in Japan
subfiles.from: Norman Ness
subfiles.about: Summarizes the events leading to the June 4 NAC decision on selling U.S. military supplies in Japan and begins considering further action.
subfiles.summary: NAC action: supplies needed under the disease-and-unrest formula versus uneconomical items; selling the first category relieves Army custody costs and payment ranks ahead of occupation costs; continues past page 80.
